note: Says he feels strain in his joints and a pull on his neck during the fall, and that gravity acts with equal force in motion or at rest and is never escaped.
Garbled mechanics of cage, rope and friction with velocity growing as the square of distance; never says what the passenger feels.
Describes the cage accelerating against brake-beam, pulley and gear friction; nothing on what is felt or on weight.
A list of textbook review questions cycling windmill, water-wheel and air-gun, then a publisher catalogue block printed twice; no answer.
Feels shock and jar as the elevator descends; explicitly says the body is not lighter than when standing and its weight works on us at every instant.
Weight rests on a yielding medium of space, the support affords no purchase, shock on hitting the ground; never says what is felt during the fall.
Gravity's pull on our weight is felt throughout, each stage deepening the impression of weight; denies that we swing loose of our weight.
The fall is a violent irregular jolt from rope slack; concludes gravity is a non-uniform force varying with distance fallen; nothing on weight felt.
Elevator falls in a serpentine course; our feet press the floor and legs give way as we are drawn along with it; gravity acts on all bodies alike.
Feet are thrust down on the floor by the descending mass and the body tends to the ground; gravity's force varies with posture.
We are drawn toward the floor and pushed along it, limbs yield to the pull of the cage, perception suspended; gravity an inexorable power.
We experience a violent shock and are bound to our position by gravity, not free to glide; the force produces the shock we feel.
Garbled projectile talk; says the elevator falls through a horizontal motion on the floor; nothing on what is felt.
The man is pressed downward by the car and pulled toward the floor; later says he falls so quietly he does not know he is descending.
Treats the cable itself as the thing falling from a tower, with iron strength and velocities; never mentions the passenger.
The pull you feel is the collected pull of elevator, car and cable; we are pressed and pulled by gravity we cannot resist.
The man's feet are fastened to the floor and his body is dragged down by a constant uniform pull of the cable and Earth.
Gravity is a continuous force acting on every body alike in proportion to mass; nothing on what the passenger feels.
Stones, millstones and parabolas; ends cut off saying a man in a well-constructed elevator does not feel the weight of the floor, which is above him; too garbled to count as weightless.
Gravity gives the cage a slow steady push and a lateral drag, energy converted to work; nothing on what the passenger feels.
Gravitation acts on every particle alike, mountain and sand grain fall by the same law; nothing on what is felt.
A chain of review questions degenerating into what if the cable breaks and what if the cable stopped any more, repeated until cut off.
Vague harmony of weight, floor resistance and air friction; gravity opposes us; a man on a platform whose feet fail to strike the floor; nothing concrete on what is felt.
As it falls the car and its load press down on the floor like a stone in a vessel; inertia and gravity conspire to a downward force.
The elevator leaps away from its support and is launched by concentrated force; earth acts on us as on a stone; nothing on what the passenger feels.
The brakeman is in great tension and every particle of his body in strain; a man walking or riding at speed carries no weight; cut off.
You feel the floor rising in front of you; suspended bodies exert a gradual pressure on the support; molecules press laterally on the floor.
The pull on your feet and legs is constant and powerfully felt as we fall; gravity draws all bodies equally.
Reads it as a grain elevator crushing grain; gravity is a uniform law drawing all bodies to the centre; nothing on what is felt.
Generic talk of gravity as a steady uniform push on carriage, horse and rider that we must submit to; nothing on the fall itself.
Gravity acts on every particle through the cable; final paragraph restates the same sentence about gravity on every particle a dozen times until cut off.
The man strikes the floor with his feet and falls back upon the car, thrown violently off his feet; gravity acts on all matter alike.
The cable yields gradually and the frame dissolves; gravity acts in proportion to weight and weights set the time of descent; nothing felt.
A carriage on a cable incline with chain and axle; gravity acts with varying intensity on a moving body; nothing on what is felt.
Stones dropped together land together; gravity differs from other forces only in being a constant persistent pull; nothing on what the passenger feels.
Cable and pulley mechanics with gravity proportional to distance squared; same law moves earth and moon; nothing on what is felt.
Cage and passengers share a common motion and gravity acts equally on every part, yet a heavier passenger falls faster; never says what is felt.
